place.zh: 沉鼎观 · 外门 · 饭堂门口
place.en: Chending Temple · The outer court · the refectory door

setup.zh: 九月初十，天没亮，饭堂门口排起了长龙：周衡发腰牌、灵石，马小宝收公中。身后有人拍你肩膀——阿禾。
setup.en: The tenth of the ninth month, before dawn, a long queue at the refectory door: Zhou Heng hands out waist tags and spirit stones, Ma Xiaobao collects the common fund. Someone taps your shoulder from behind — Ah He.

recap.zh: 入门第二天，阿禾下山来找你——昨天测出木天灵根，观主收了亲传；外门的灰袍底下露着一线青，「青的扎眼」。她在小本子上记了你一笔：下下之资——「哪天你不是了，好对账」。
recap.en: Your second day in the sect, Ah He came down the mountain to find you — yesterday a wood heaven root, taken by the abbot as his own disciple; a thread of green showing under a borrowed outer-court grey robe ("green stands out"). She wrote you into her notebook: bottom of the bottom — "the day you're not, we check the books."

zh: 九月初十，饭堂门口，领灵石，交公中。
身后有人拍你的肩膀——一个红鼻头。
en: The tenth of the ninth month, the refectory door: draw stones, pay the common fund.
Someone taps your shoulder — a red nose.
"The day you're not, we check the books."

story.zh:
沉鼎山外门的日子，沈小满是从交钱开始过的——钱还没捂热，便有人伸手来收。九月初十，天还没亮透。外门几十间灰瓦房顺着东坡一层一层叠上去，瓦楞上浮着一层白气——不是炊烟，是山里的灵气夜里沉下来，叫早上的风一赶，贴着屋脊慢慢地流。饭堂门口已排起了长龙。一百来个新弟子，穿着昨夜才领的灰袍，袍子是照着大个子裁的，小个子穿上，下摆拖到脚面，远远看过去，像一群刚出窝的灰鸭子。

饭堂门口摆一张榆木桌子，桌子后面坐着外门执事周衡。周衡是个三十来岁的瘦高个儿，一脸愁苦，面前摊着一本厚得能当枕头使的账簿，叫一个名字，发一块枣木腰牌，三块灵石。那灵石有鸽子蛋大小，石皮发灰，里头却隐隐透出一点光来，像雪地里埋着的一粒火星。周衡发一个人，便抬头看那人一眼，道一声：「有前途！」发到第三十几个，那三个字已经说得像念经。轮到小满，他看了看名册上「五行杂灵根」那几个字，端详了小满好一会儿，道：「……有前途。」没有那个叹号。

进了饭堂的门，往前走不上十步，又是一张桌子。桌子后面坐着马小宝，面前摆一只描金的小木匣，匣上贴一张红纸，写着两个大字：**公中**。他身后站着两个进门三年的老弟子，抱着胳膊，像庙门口的两尊泥塑。唱名的那个执事——码头上冲白衣人点头、正殿里替马小宝添了一道的那一个——是马三的表哥，马小宝的表伯；一夜之间，马小宝便成了「马师兄」。周衡瞧了那匣子一眼，低头接着发——名册在唱名执事手里。排在小满前头的孙二狗，背上还背着那个比他身子还大的包袱，捧着三块灵石看了半天，拣出最小的一块，哆哆嗦嗦地放进了匣子。他刚要走，身后那尊泥塑伸出一条腿来，在他脚后跟上一勾，他背着那个大包袱往前一栽，脚下踉跄了三四步，歪歪斜斜，像一根给风吹弯了的芦苇，弯到了地皮上，偏偏又弹了回来——竟没有倒。

小满拣了一块不大不小的，放进匣子里。马小宝眯起眼睛：「就这么交了？」小满道：「规矩嘛。小宝哥辛苦。」马小宝道：「叫马师兄。」小满道：「马师兄辛苦。」马小宝满意地一扬下巴，腰上一块旧木牌晃了一晃，一面刻着「巡夜」两个字——外门没人肯接的差事，他表伯偏偏派给了他。小满凑得近，鼻子里忽然钻进一股味儿：不是桂花糕的甜，是一股青苦的草腥气，凉丝丝的，吸进去，肚子底下那口枯井，竟像给凉水激了一下。马小宝一夜巡回来，身上带的就是这个。

身后忽然有人拍他肩膀。

小满回头一看，是一个扎两根小辫子的姑娘，灰袍比他的还大一号，袖子挽了三道，下摆拿草绳在腰里扎了一圈；领口底下，露出一线青。一个红鼻头，冻得像一根萝卜。手里捏着一个巴掌大的小本子，一截炭条夹在耳朵上。

小满道：「……阿禾。你躲了我一整天。」

阿禾道：「嗯。」

「你怎么下来了？观主的院子在山顶上。」

「走下来的。」阿禾道，「石阶上，我从你边上冲过去的。洛书，我比你先摆好半炷香。」她顿了一顿，一本正经地道，「考试的时候，不认人。认了你，要分心。」小满道：「那现在呢？」阿禾道：「现在考完了。」

小满瞧了瞧她领口那一线青，又瞧了瞧她身上这件灰袍——外门的。「你这身……」阿禾把领口往上拽了一拽：「借的。青的扎眼。」她往饭堂里头瞟了一眼。唱名的那个执事坐在马小宝身后，端着茶碗，眼睛在新弟子脸上一张一张地过。

小满问：「你怎么没跟我一起来？」

阿禾道：「我娘说，你一个人去，会死。我一个人去，也会死。两个人一起去，死一双，不划算。所以分开走。」小满想了一想，觉得这话虽然难听，账倒是算得明白。阿禾舔了舔炭条，又记了一笔，道：「下下之资。」
story.en:
Shen Xiaoman's days in the outer court of Mount Chending began with paying money — before the money was even warm, someone held out a hand for it. The tenth of the ninth month, before it was properly light. The outer court's few dozen grey-tiled houses climbed the east slope tier on tier, and a white breath floated over their tiles — not cooking smoke: the mountain's spirit qi, settled in the night, herded by the morning wind and flowing slowly along the ridgepoles. A long line had already formed at the refectory door. A hundred-odd new disciples in the grey robes handed out only last night — robes cut for big boys, so on the small ones the hems trailed on their feet; seen from a distance, like a brood of grey ducklings just out of the nest.

At the refectory door stood an elm table, and behind it sat the outer-court steward Zhou Heng — a tall thin man of thirty or so with a careworn face, before him a ledger thick enough to sleep on. He called a name and handed out a jujube-wood waist token and three spirit stones. The stones were the size of a pigeon's egg, grey-skinned, yet a faint light showed inside, like a spark buried in snow. With each one he looked up at the disciple and said: "Promising!" By the thirtieth-odd the word had become a chant. When it was Xiaoman's turn he looked at "five-element mixed root" in the register and studied Xiaoman a long while. "…Promising." Without the exclamation mark.

Inside the refectory door, not ten steps on, was another table. Behind it sat Ma Xiaobao with a little gilt box in front of him, a strip of red paper pasted on it bearing two big characters: **COMMON FUND**. Behind him stood two old disciples three years in, arms folded, like the clay guardians at a temple gate. The roll-calling steward — the one who had nodded to the man in white on the flats, and who had added Ma Xiaobao's missing stroke himself in the main hall — was Ma San's elder cousin — Ma Xiaobao's uncle; overnight Ma Xiaobao had become "Senior Brother Ma." Zhou Heng glanced at that box, lowered his head and went on handing out — the register was in the roll-calling steward's hands. Ahead of Xiaoman was Sun Ergou, still carrying that bundle bigger than himself; he held his three stones and looked at them a long while, picked out the smallest, and set it trembling in the box. He was just moving off when one of the clay guardians stuck out a leg and hooked his heel; with the big bundle on his back he pitched forward, staggered three or four steps, swaying every which way, like a reed blown flat by the wind, bent right down to the ground — and sprang back up. He didn't fall.

Xiaoman chose one neither big nor small and put it in the box. Ma Xiaobao narrowed his eyes. "Just like that?" Xiaoman said, "Rules are rules. Thank you for your trouble, Brother Xiaobao." Ma Xiaobao said, "Senior Brother Ma." Xiaoman said, "Thank you for your trouble, Senior Brother Ma." Ma Xiaobao lifted his chin, satisfied, and an old wooden token swung at his waist, one face carved NIGHT WATCH — a post nobody in the outer court would take, which his uncle had gone out of his way to give him. Xiaoman was close, and a smell slipped into his nose: not the sweetness of osmanthus cake but a green, bitter, grassy smell, cool; breathing it in, the dry well beneath his belly felt splashed with cold water. Ma Xiaobao came back from a night's watch carrying this on him.

Someone tapped him on the shoulder from behind.

Xiaoman turned. It was a girl with two little braids, her grey robe a size bigger even than his, the sleeves rolled three times, the hem tied round her waist with straw rope; under the collar showed a thread of green. A red nose, frozen like a radish. In her hand a notebook no bigger than a palm; a stick of charcoal tucked behind her ear.

Xiaoman said, "…Ah He. You dodged me all day."

"Mm," said Ah He.

"What are you doing down here? The abbot's court is at the top of the mountain."

"Walked down," said Ah He. "On the stair, I ran past you. The Luo diagram, I finished half a stick of incense before you." She paused, and said very seriously, "In an exam you don't know anyone. Know you, and I'm distracted." Xiaoman said, "And now?" Ah He said, "Now the exam's over."

Xiaoman looked at the thread of green at her collar, then at the grey robe she had on — an outer-court one. "What's this you're…" Ah He tugged the collar up. "Borrowed. Green stands out." She glanced into the refectory. The steward who had called the names sat behind Ma Xiaobao with a teacup, his eyes passing over the new disciples' faces one by one.

Xiaoman asked, "Why didn't you come with me?"

Ah He said, "My mum said, if you go alone you'll die. If I go alone I'll die too. If we go together, two die — bad bargain. So we went separately." Xiaoman thought it over: it sounded awful, but the sums were right. Ah He licked her charcoal, made another note, and said: "Lowest of the low."

exits.means: lets Ah He's entry stand and means to prove it wrong, goes on to the lesson

what.zh: 外门第一天，阿禾在小本子上记了你一笔：下下之资。你说：哪天不是了，拿本子来对。
what.en: Your first day in the outer court: Ah He wrote you into the little notebook — bottom of the class. You said: the day it isn't so, bring the notebook.

story.zh:
小满想了一想，道：「记吧。哪天我不是了，你拿本子来对。」

阿禾点了点头，像是他总算说了一句像样的话。她转身往山上走了。

小满站在原地，瞧着她那两截小辫子一跳一跳地走远了，心里头说不出是什么滋味。他想起出门那天，老槐树底下只站着他娘一个人。他那时候还道这丫头在睡懒觉。

原来她早走了一天，走的是另一条路。如今她走的，还是另一条路——往山顶上去。

那几天，小满逢人便问一句：太华山多远？孙二狗不知道。讲堂上一个老弟子听见了，笑他：「西边，两千来里，雍州。太华山上的太一宫。你问它做什么？」小满没说做什么。
story.en:
Xiaoman thought it over and said, "Write it down. The day I'm not, bring the notebook and we'll check."

Ah He nodded, as if he had finally said something sensible. She turned and went off up the mountain.

Xiaoman stood where he was and watched her two little braids bob away, and could not have said what he felt. He remembered the day he left: under the old locust tree there had been only his mother. He had supposed the girl was sleeping in.

So she had gone a day early, by another road. And she was on another road still — the one up to the summit.

For the next few days Xiaoman asked everyone the same thing: how far is Mount Taihua? Sun Ergou didn't know. An older disciple in the lecture hall overheard and laughed at him. "West. Two thousand li and more, in Yongzhou. The Taiyi Palace, up on Mount Taihua. What do you want with it?" Xiaoman didn't say.

exits.means: balks at being written down; she keeps it to check later

what.zh: 外门第一天，阿禾在小本子上记了你一笔：下下之资。「哪天你不是了，好对账。」
what.en: Your first day in the outer court: Ah He wrote you into the little notebook — bottom of the class. "The day you're not, we check the books."

story.zh:
小满道：「这也记？」

阿禾道：「记着。哪天你不是了，好对账。」她转身往山上走了。

小满瞧着她那两截小辫子一跳一跳地走远了，心里头说不出是什么滋味。出门那天，老槐树底下只站着他娘一个人，他还道这丫头在睡懒觉。原来她早走了一天，走的是另一条路。如今她走的，还是另一条路——往山顶上去。

那几天，小满逢人便问一句：太华山多远？孙二狗不知道。讲堂上一个老弟子听见了，笑他：「西边，两千来里，雍州。太华山上的太一宫。你问它做什么？」小满没说做什么。
story.en:
"You're writing that down too?" said Xiaoman.

"I'm keeping it," said Ah He. "The day you're not, we check the books." She turned and went off up the mountain.

Xiaoman watched her two braids bob away and couldn't have said what he felt. The day he left, only his mother had stood under the old locust tree, and he'd thought this girl was sleeping in. She had left a day earlier, by another road. She was on another road still — the one up to the summit.

For the next few days Xiaoman asked everyone the same thing: how far is Mount Taihua? Sun Ergou didn't know. An older disciple in the lecture hall overheard and laughed at him. "West. Two thousand li and more, in Yongzhou. The Taiyi Palace, up on Mount Taihua. What do you want with it?" Xiaoman didn't say.
